content:
The image shows a soybean leaf with:
- Numerous small, dark brown to reddish-purple/black spots scattered across the leaf surface
- Some spots with yellow halos visible
- Lesions appear on both the upper and lower leaf surfaces
- Spots are small, irregular in shape, and distributed across the leaf
- Some coalescence of lesions into larger irregular blotches
- The pattern starts as small dark specks progressing to larger necrotic areas

This pattern — small, dark brown irregularly shaped lesions on both leaf surfaces, with some yellow halos, and lesions coalescing into larger blotches — is characteristic of **Septoria brown spot**. The lesions match the description: "small, irregularly shaped dark brown lesions on both leaf surfaces; adjacent lesions coalesce into larger irregular blotches." The purple-brown coloration of the spots also aligns well with Septoria.

The yellow halos on some spots could suggest Bacterial Blight, but those lesions are typically more angular and water-soaked. The dense scattering of small dark spots coalescing is more consistent with Septoria brown spot.
